    exact E.symm
  | add a d ha hd => simp only [MulOpposite.op_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, ha, hd]
  | smul z a ha => simp only [MulOpposite.op_smul, map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, ha]

private theorem wordPair_ext {M : Type (max u v)} [AddCommGroup M] [Module Complex M]
    {f g : wordBimod.{u,v} (p.tensor q) →ₗ[Complex] M}
    (h : ∀ b c, f (wordPair p q b c) = g (wordPair p q b c)) : f = g := by
  let t := ((LinearMap.llcomp Complex _ _ _) f).comp (wordPair p q)
  have ht (a : MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p) (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) :
      t (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a) b) c =
        t b (leftHom (wordBimod q) a c) := by
    change f (wordPair p q (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a) b) c) =
      f (wordPair p q b (leftHom (wordBimod q) a c))
    rw [wordPair_middle p q]
  obtain ⟨_, _, uniq⟩ := wordPairUP p q t ht
  exact (uniq f (fun _ _ => rfl)).trans (uniq g (fun b c => (h b c).symm)).symm

private noncomputable def forwardTriple (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] wordBimod.{u,v} q →ₗ[Complex]
      V X →ₗ[Complex] V ((T q ⋙ T p).obj X) :=
  { toFun := fun b => ((LinearMap.llcomp Complex _ _ _)
        (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b)).comp (pure (wordBimod q) X)
    map_add' := fun b d => by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro c
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro x
      simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.llcomp_apply]
    map_smul' := fun z b => by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro c
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro x
      simp only [RingHom.id_apply, map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply,
        LinearMap.llcomp_apply] }

private theorem forwardTriple_balanced (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (a : MonoidAlgebra Complex L)
    (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p) (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) :
    forwardTriple p q X (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a) b) c =
      forwardTriple p q X b (leftHom (wordBimod q) a c) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  change pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a) b)
      (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) =
    pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X (leftHom (wordBimod q) a c) x)
  rw [(universal (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X)).1.2 a b,
    (universal (wordBimod q) X).1.1 a c]

private noncomputable def forwardPairing (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    wordBimod.{u,v} (p.tensor q) →ₗ[Complex] V X →ₗ[Complex] V ((T q ⋙ T p).obj X) :=
  Classical.choose ((wordPairUP p q (forwardTriple p q X) (forwardTriple_balanced p q X)).exists)

private theorem forwardPairing_pure (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    forwardPairing p q X (wordPair p q b c) x =
      pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) := by
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun
    (Classical.choose_spec ((wordPairUP p q (forwardTriple p q X)
      (forwardTriple_balanced p q X)).exists) b c) x

private theorem forwardPairing_balanced (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    Balanced (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X ((T q ⋙ T p).obj X) (forwardPairing p q X) := by
  constructor
  · intro a d x
    let Y := (T q ⋙ T p).obj X
    let act : V Y →ₗ[Complex] V Y := RestrictScalars.lsmul Complex (MonoidAlgebra Complex K) Y a
    have e : ((forwardPairing p q X).flip x).comp (leftHom (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) a) =
        act.comp ((forwardPairing p q X).flip x) := by
      apply wordPair_ext p q
      intro b c
      change forwardPairing p q X (leftHom (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) a (wordPair p q b c)) x =
        a • (show Y from forwardPairing p q X (wordPair p q b c) x)
      rw [← wordPair_left p q, forwardPairing_pure, forwardPairing_pure]
      exact (universal (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X)).1.1 a b _
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun e d
  · intro a d x
    have e : ((forwardPairing p q X).flip x).comp
        (rightHom (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) (MulOpposite.op a)) =
        (forwardPairing p q X).flip (a • (show X from x)) := by
      apply wordPair_ext p q
      intro b c
      change forwardPairing p q X (rightHom (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) (MulOpposite.op a)
        (wordPair p q b c)) x = forwardPairing p q X (wordPair p q b c) (a • (show X from x))
      rw [← wordPair_right p q, forwardPairing_pure, forwardPairing_pure,
        (universal (wordBimod q) X).1.2 a c x]
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun e d

private noncomputable def compHom (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    (T (p.tensor q)).obj X ⟶ (T q ⋙ T p).obj X :=
  Classical.choose (((universal (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).2 _
    (forwardPairing p q X) (forwardPairing_balanced p q X)).exists)

private theorem compHom_pure (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    VMap (compHom p q X) (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x) =
      pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) :=
  (Classical.choose_spec (((universal (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).2 _
    (forwardPairing p q X) (forwardPairing_balanced p q X)).exists) (wordPair p q b c) x).trans
      (forwardPairing_pure p q X b c x)

-- Right multiplication on the source gives a left action on the space of linear maps.
private noncomputable def homAction (Y : Mod.{u,v} K) :
    MonoidAlgebra Complex L →+* Module.End Complex (wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V Y) where
  toFun a := LinearMap.lcomp Complex (V Y) (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a))
  map_zero' := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro f
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, MulOpposite.op_zero, map_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]
  map_one' := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro f
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, MulOpposite.op_one, map_one, one_apply_eq_self]
  map_add' a d := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro f
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, MulOpposite.op_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]
  map_mul' a d := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro f
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, MulOpposite.op_mul, map_mul, mul_apply_eq_comp]

private noncomputable def homMod (Y : Mod.{u,v} K) : Mod.{u,v} L := by
  letI : Module (MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V Y) :=
    Module.compHom _ (homAction p Y)
  exact ModuleCat.of (GC L) (wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V Y)

private theorem homMod_smul (Y : Mod.{u,v} K) (a : MonoidAlgebra Complex L)
    (f : homMod p Y) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p) :
    (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V Y from a • f) b =
      (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V Y from f)
        (rightHom (wordBimod p) (MulOpposite.op a) b) := rfl

private noncomputable def inverseTriple (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] wordBimod.{u,v} q →ₗ[Complex]
      V X →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) :=
  ((LinearMap.llcomp Complex _ _ _) (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X)).comp (wordPair p q)

private noncomputable def inverseCurry (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : X) :
    homMod p ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) :=
  ((inverseTriple p q X).flip c).flip x

private theorem inverseCurry_apply (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) from inverseCurry p q X c x) b =
      pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x := rfl

private theorem inverseInner_exists (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    ∃ g : (T q).obj X →ₗ[MonoidAlgebra Complex L] homMod p ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X),
      ∀ c x, g (rawPure (wordBimod q) X c x) = inverseCurry p q X c x := by
  apply ((rawUniversal (wordBimod q) X).2 _ (inverseCurry p q X) ?_).exists
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro c d x
    change ((inverseTriple p q X).flip (c + d)).flip x =
      ((inverseTriple p q X).flip c).flip x + ((inverseTriple p q X).flip d).flip x
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.flip_apply, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]
  · intro c x y
    change ((inverseTriple p q X).flip c).flip (x + y) =
      ((inverseTriple p q X).flip c).flip x + ((inverseTriple p q X).flip c).flip y
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    simp only [LinearMap.flip_apply, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]
  · intro a c x
    change inverseCurry p q X (leftHom (wordBimod q) a c) x = a • inverseCurry p q X c x
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    rw [homMod_smul, inverseCurry_apply, inverseCurry_apply, wordPair_middle p q]
  · intro a c x
    change inverseCurry p q X (rightHom (wordBimod q) (MulOpposite.op a) c) x =
      inverseCurry p q X c (a • x)
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    rw [inverseCurry_apply, inverseCurry_apply, wordPair_right p q,
      (universal (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).1.2]

private noncomputable def inverseInner (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    V ((T q).obj X) →ₗ[Complex] wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) where
  toFun y :=
    let g := Classical.choose (inverseInner_exists p q X)
    g (show (T q).obj X from y)
  map_add' y z := by
    let g := Classical.choose (inverseInner_exists p q X)
    exact g.map_add (show (T q).obj X from y) (show (T q).obj X from z)
  map_smul' z y := by
    let g := Classical.choose (inverseInner_exists p q X)
    have e := g.map_smul (algebraMap Complex (GC L) z) (show (T q).obj X from y)
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro b
    change (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) from
        g ((algebraMap Complex (GC L) z) • (show (T q).obj X from y))) b =
      z • (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) from g y) b
    rw [e, homMod_smul, rightHom_scalar, map_smul]

private theorem inverseInner_pure (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    inverseInner p q X (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) b =
      pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x := by
  exact (congrArg (fun f : homMod p ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) =>
    (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) from f) b)
    (Classical.choose_spec (inverseInner_exists p q X) c x)).trans (inverseCurry_apply p q X b c x)

private theorem inverseInner_balanced (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    Balanced (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) (inverseInner p q X).flip := by
  constructor
  · intro a b y
    let Y := (T (p.tensor q)).obj X
    let act : V Y →ₗ[Complex] V Y := RestrictScalars.lsmul Complex (MonoidAlgebra Complex K) Y a
    have e : (inverseInner p q X).flip (leftHom (wordBimod p) a b) =
        act.comp ((inverseInner p q X).flip b) := by
      apply pure_linear_ext (wordBimod q) X
      intro c x
      change inverseInner p q X (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) (leftHom (wordBimod p) a b) =
        a • (show Y from inverseInner p q X (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) b)
      rw [inverseInner_pure, inverseInner_pure, wordPair_left p q,
        (universal (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).1.1]
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun e y
  · intro a b y
    let g := Classical.choose (inverseInner_exists p q X)
    have e := g.map_smul a (show (T q).obj X from y)
    exact (congrArg (fun f : homMod p ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) =>
      (show wordBimod.{u,v} p →ₗ[Complex] V ((T (p.tensor q)).obj X) from f) b) e).symm

private noncomputable def compInv (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    (T q ⋙ T p).obj X ⟶ (T (p.tensor q)).obj X :=
  Classical.choose (((universal (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X)).2 _
    (inverseInner p q X).flip (inverseInner_balanced p q X)).exists)

private theorem compInv_pure (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    VMap (compInv p q X) (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x)) =
      pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x :=
  (Classical.choose_spec (((universal (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X)).2 _
    (inverseInner p q X).flip (inverseInner_balanced p q X)).exists) b
      (pure (wordBimod q) X c x)).trans (inverseInner_pure p q X b c x)

private theorem word_tensor_hom_ext (X : Mod.{u,v} H) {Y : Mod.{u,v} K}
    {f g : (T (p.tensor q)).obj X ⟶ Y}
    (eq : ∀ b c x,
      VMap f (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x) =
      VMap g (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x)) : f = g := by
  apply hom_ext_pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X
  intro d x
  have e : (VMap f).comp ((pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).flip x) =
      (VMap g).comp ((pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X).flip x) := by
    apply wordPair_ext p q
    intro b c
    exact eq b c x
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun e d

private theorem nested_tensor_hom_ext (X : Mod.{u,v} H) {Y : Mod.{u,v} K}
    {f g : (T q ⋙ T p).obj X ⟶ Y}
    (eq : ∀ b c x,
      VMap f (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x)) =
      VMap g (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x))) : f = g := by
  apply hom_ext_pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X)
  intro b y
  have e : (VMap f).comp (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b) =
      (VMap g).comp (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b) := by
    apply pure_linear_ext (wordBimod q) X
    intro c x
    exact eq b c x
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun e y

private noncomputable def compApp (X : Mod.{u,v} H) :
    (T (p.tensor q)).obj X ≅ (T q ⋙ T p).obj X where
  hom := compHom p q X
  inv := compInv p q X
  hom_inv_id := by
    apply word_tensor_hom_ext p q X
    intro b c x
    change VMap (compInv p q X)
      (VMap (compHom p q X) (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X (wordPair p q b c) x)) = _
    rw [compHom_pure, compInv_pure] <;> rfl
  inv_hom_id := by
    apply nested_tensor_hom_ext p q X
    intro b c x
    change VMap (compHom p q X)
      (VMap (compInv p q X) (pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x))) = _
    rw [compInv_pure, compHom_pure] <;> rfl

private noncomputable def compIso :
    T (p.tensor q) ≅ T q ⋙ T p :=
  NatIso.ofComponents (compApp p q) (by
    intro X Y f
    apply word_tensor_hom_ext p q X
    intro b c x
    let P := wordBimod.{u,v} p
    let Q := wordBimod.{u,v} q
    let R := wordBimod.{u,v} (p.tensor q)
    change VMap (compHom p q Y)
        (((tensor R).map f).hom (rawPure R X (wordPair p q b c) x)) =
      ((tensor P).map ((tensor Q).map f)).hom
        (VMap (compHom p q X) (pure R X (wordPair p q b c) x))
    have eR := rawMapInput R f (wordPair p q b c) x
    have eQ := rawMapInput Q f c x
    have eP := rawMapInput P ((tensor Q).map f) b (rawPure Q X c x)
    calc
      _ = VMap (compHom p q Y) (pure R Y (wordPair p q b c) (f.hom x)) :=
        congrArg (VMap (compHom p q Y)) eR
      _ = rawPure P ((tensor Q).obj Y) b (rawPure Q Y c (f.hom x)) :=
        compHom_pure p q Y b c (f.hom x)
      _ = rawPure P ((tensor Q).obj Y) b (((tensor Q).map f).hom (rawPure Q X c x)) :=
        congrArg (rawPure P ((tensor Q).obj Y) b) eQ.symm
      _ = ((tensor P).map ((tensor Q).map f)).hom (rawPure P ((tensor Q).obj X) b (rawPure Q X c x)) :=
        eP.symm
      _ = _ := congrArg (((tensor P).map ((tensor Q).map f)).hom) (compHom_pure p q X b c x).symm)

private theorem compIso_pure (X : Mod.{u,v} H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} p)
    (c : wordBimod.{u,v} q) (x : V X) :
    VMap ((compIso p q).hom.app X)
      (pure (wordBimod (p.tensor q)) X
        ((lower (p.tensor q)).symm (Biset.pairLinear Complex p.basis q.basis (lower p b) (lower q c))) x) =
      pure (wordBimod p) ((T q).obj X) b (pure (wordBimod q) X c x) :=
  compHom_pure p q X b c x

#print axioms compIso_pure

end WordComposition

  {σ : ∀ X : ModuleCat.{w} R, N → X → F.obj X}
  {τ : ∀ X : ModuleCat.{w} R, P → X → G.obj X}

omit [Module Complex N] in
private theorem strand_hom_ext (hσ : StrandPresentation lN rN σ)
    {X : ModuleCat.{w} R} {Y : ModuleCat.{w} S} {f g : F.obj X ⟶ Y}
    (h : ∀ n x, f.hom (σ X n x) = g.hom (σ X n x)) : f = g := by
  have hb := hσ.1 X
  have hg : StrandBalanced lN rN X Y (fun n x => g.hom (σ X n x)) :=
    ⟨fun n m x => (congrArg g.hom (hb.1 n m x)).trans (g.hom.map_add _ _),
     fun n x y => (congrArg g.hom (hb.2.1 n x y)).trans (g.hom.map_add _ _),
     fun s n x => (congrArg g.hom (hb.2.2.1 s n x)).trans (g.hom.map_smul s _),
     fun r n x => congrArg g.hom (hb.2.2.2 r n x)⟩
  obtain ⟨lift, _, uniq⟩ := hσ.2.1 X Y _ hg
  exact ModuleCat.hom_injective ((uniq f.hom h).trans (uniq g.hom (fun _ _ => rfl)).symm)

variable (e : N ≃ₗ[Complex] P)
    (el : ∀ s n, e (lN s n) = lP s (e n))
    (er : ∀ r n, e (rN r n) = rP r (e n))
    (hσ : StrandPresentation lN rN σ) (hτ : StrandPresentation lP rP τ)

include el er hσ hτ in
private theorem strand_component_exists (X : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    ∃! f : F.obj X →ₗ[S] G.obj X, ∀ n x, f (σ X n x) = τ X (e n) x := by
  have hb := hτ.1 X
  apply hσ.2.1 X (G.obj X) (fun n x => τ X (e n) x)
  refine ⟨?_, fun n x y => hb.2.1 (e n) x y, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro n m x
    simpa only [e.map_add] using hb.1 (e n) (e m) x
  · intro s n x
    simpa only [el] using hb.2.2.1 s (e n) x
  · intro r n x
    simpa only [er] using hb.2.2.2 r (e n) x

private noncomputable def strand_component (X : ModuleCat.{w} R) : F.obj X ⟶ G.obj X :=
  ModuleCat.ofHom (Classical.choose (strand_component_exists e el er hσ hτ X))

private theorem strand_component_pure (X : ModuleCat.{w} R) (n : N) (x : X) :
    (strand_component e el er hσ hτ X).hom (σ X n x) = τ X (e n) x :=
  (Classical.choose_spec (strand_component_exists e el er hσ hτ X)).1 n x

private noncomputable def strand_hom : F ⟶ G where
  app := strand_component e el er hσ hτ
  naturality {X Y} f := by
    apply strand_hom_ext hσ
    intro n x
    change (strand_component e el er hσ hτ Y).hom ((F.map f).hom (σ X n x)) =
      (G.map f).hom ((strand_component e el er hσ hτ X).hom (σ X n x))
    rw [hσ.2.2, strand_component_pure, strand_component_pure, hτ.2.2]

private theorem strand_hom_pure (X : ModuleCat.{w} R) (n : N) (x : X) :
    ((strand_hom e el er hσ hτ).app X).hom (σ X n x) = τ X (e n) x :=
  strand_component_pure e el er hσ hτ X n x

include el in
private theorem strand_symm_left (s : S) (p : P) :
    e.symm (lP s p) = lN s (e.symm p) :=
  e.injective (by rw [e.apply_symm_apply, el, e.apply_symm_apply])

include er in
private theorem strand_symm_right (r : R) (p : P) :
    e.symm (rP r p) = rN r (e.symm p) :=
  e.injective (by rw [e.apply_symm_apply, er, e.apply_symm_apply])

private noncomputable def strand_iso : F ≅ G where
  hom := strand_hom e el er hσ hτ
  inv := strand_hom e.symm (strand_symm_left e el) (strand_symm_right e er) hτ hσ
  hom_inv_id := by
    apply NatTrans.ext
    funext X
    apply strand_hom_ext hσ
    intro n x
    change ((strand_hom e.symm _ _ hτ hσ).app X).hom
        (((strand_hom e el er hσ hτ).app X).hom (σ X n x)) = σ X n x
    rw [strand_hom_pure, strand_hom_pure, e.symm_apply_apply]
  inv_hom_id := by
    apply NatTrans.ext
    funext X
    apply strand_hom_ext hτ
    intro p x
    change ((strand_hom e el er hσ hτ).app X).hom
        (((strand_hom e.symm _ _ hτ hσ).app X).hom (τ X p x)) = τ X p x
    rw [strand_hom_pure, strand_hom_pure, e.apply_symm_apply]

private theorem strand_iso_pure (X : ModuleCat.{w} R) (n : N) (x : X) :
    ((strand_iso e el er hσ hτ).hom.app X).hom (σ X n x) = τ X (e n) x :=
  strand_hom_pure e el er hσ hτ X n x

end Compare

end DiagramFunctorProof

namespace DiagramFunctorProof

open CategoryTheory

universe u v

variable {U : Type u} [Group U]

private noncomputable def wordCoeffIso {K H G : Subgroup U} (p : Word K H)
    (h : p.basis.carrier = G) : wordBimod.{u,v} p ≃ₗ[Complex] MonoidAlgebra Complex G :=
  let coeff : (G →₀ Complex) ≃ₗ[Complex] MonoidAlgebra Complex G :=
    (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv Complex).symm
  (lower p).trans (cast (congrArg (fun C : Type u =>
    (C →₀ Complex) ≃ₗ[Complex] MonoidAlgebra Complex G) h.symm) coeff)

private theorem wordPresentation {K H : Subgroup U} (p : Word K H) :
    StrandPresentation (fun s b => leftHom (wordBimod.{u,v} p) s b)
      (fun r => rightHom (wordBimod.{u,v} p) (MulOpposite.op r))
      (rawPure (wordBimod.{u,v} p)) :=
  ⟨fun X => (rawUniversal (wordBimod p) X).1,
   fun X => (rawUniversal (wordBimod p) X).2,
   fun _ _ => rawMapInput (wordBimod p)⟩

private theorem strandActions {K H : Type u} [Group K] [Group H]
    {B : BM.{u,v} K H} {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra Complex A]
    (e : B ≃ₗ[Complex] A) (L : MonoidAlgebra Complex K →ₐ[Complex] A)
    (R : MonoidAlgebra Complex H →ₐ[Complex] A)
    (h : ∀ k h b, e (B.ρ (k, h⁻¹) b) =
      L (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex K k) * (e b * R (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex H h))) :
    (∀ s b, e (leftHom B s b) = L s * e b) ∧
    (∀ r b, e (rightHom B (MulOpposite.op r) b) = e b * R r) := by
  constructor
  · intro s b
    induction s using MonoidAlgebra.induction_on with
    | of k =>
        rw [left_of]
        simpa only [inv_one, map_one, mul_one] using h k 1 b
    | add a a' ha ha' => simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, add_mul, ha, ha']
    | smul z a ha => simp only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, smul_mul_assoc, ha]
  · intro r b
    induction r using MonoidAlgebra.induction_on with
    | of h' =>
        rw [right_of]
        simpa only [map_one, one_mul] using h 1 h' b
    | add a a' ha ha' =>
        simp only [MulOpposite.op_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, mul_add, ha, ha']
    | smul z a ha =>
        simp only [MulOpposite.op_smul, map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply, mul_smul_comm, ha]

private theorem regularWord_group (H : Subgroup U) (k h : H)
    (x : MonoidAlgebra Complex H) :
    MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
      (Finsupp.lmapDomain Complex Complex (fun z : H => k * z * h) x.coeff) =
      MonoidAlgebra.single k 1 * (x * MonoidAlgebra.single h 1) := by
  induction x using MonoidAlgebra.induction_on with
  | of z =>
      simp [MonoidAlgebra.of_apply, Finsupp.lmapDomain_apply,
        MonoidAlgebra.single_mul_single, mul_assoc]
  | add x y hx hy =>
      simp only [MonoidAlgebra.coeff_add, map_add, MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff_add, add_mul,
        mul_add, hx, hy]
  | smul r x hx =>
      simp only [MonoidAlgebra.coeff_smul, map_smul, MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff_smul,
        smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, hx]

private theorem regularWord_actions (H : Subgroup U) :
    let e := wordCoeffIso.{u,v} (G := H) (Word.empty H) rfl
    (∀ s b, e (leftHom (wordBimod (Word.empty H)) s b) = s * e b) ∧
    (∀ r b, e (rightHom (wordBimod (Word.empty H)) (MulOpposite.op r) b) = e b * r) := by
  let p := Word.empty H
  let e := wordCoeffIso.{u,v} (G := H) p rfl
  apply strandActions e (AlgHom.id _ _) (AlgHom.id _ _)
  intro k h b
  change MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
      (Finsupp.lmapDomain Complex Complex (fun z : H => k * z * (h⁻¹)⁻¹) (lower p b)) =
    MonoidAlgebra.single k 1 * ((e b) * MonoidAlgebra.single h 1)
  rw [inv_inv]
  exact regularWord_group H k h (e b)

private theorem identityPresentation (H : Subgroup U) :
    StrandPresentation (F := 𝟭 (Mod.{u,v} H))
      (fun (s b : MonoidAlgebra Complex H) => s * b) (fun r b => b * r)
      (fun X b x => b • x) := by
  refine ⟨fun X => ⟨fun n m x => add_smul n m x, fun n x y => smul_add n x y,
    fun s n x => mul_smul s n x, fun r n x => mul_smul n r x⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro X Y t ht
    have at_one (b : MonoidAlgebra Complex H) (x : X) : t b x = t 1 (b • x) := by
      simpa only [one_mul] using ht.2.2.2 b 1 x
    let f : X →ₗ[MonoidAlgebra Complex H] Y :=
      { toFun := t 1
        map_add' := ht.2.1 1
        map_smul' := fun r x => by
          change t 1 (r • x) = r • t 1 x
          rw [← at_one]
          simpa only [mul_one] using ht.2.2.1 r 1 x }
    refine ⟨f, fun b x => (at_one b x).symm, ?_⟩
    intro g hg
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    change g x = t 1 x
    simpa only [one_smul] using hg 1 x
  · intro X Y f b x
    exact f.hom.map_smul b x

private noncomputable def emptyIso (H : Subgroup U) :
    T.{u,v} (Word.empty H) ≅ 𝟭 (Mod.{u,v} H) :=
  strand_iso (wordCoeffIso (G := H) (Word.empty H) rfl)
    (regularWord_actions H).1 (regularWord_actions H).2
    (wordPresentation (Word.empty H)) (identityPresentation H)

private theorem emptyIso_pure (H : Subgroup U) (X : Mod.{u,v} H)
    (b : wordBimod.{u,v} (Word.empty H)) (x : V X) :
    VMap ((emptyIso H).hom.app X) (DiagramFunctorProof.pure (wordBimod (Word.empty H)) X b x) =
      (MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff (lower (Word.empty H) b) : MonoidAlgebra Complex H) • (show X from x) :=
  strand_iso_pure (wordCoeffIso (G := H) (Word.empty H) rfl)
    (regularWord_actions H).1 (regularWord_actions H).2
    (wordPresentation (Word.empty H)) (identityPresentation H) X b x

private noncomputable abbrev strandPhi {H G : Subgroup U} (a : ConjEmbedding H G) :=
  MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex a.toHom

private noncomputable abbrev strandInd {H G : Subgroup U} (a : ConjEmbedding H G) :
    Func.{u,v} G H :=
  (Rep.ofModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := Complex) (G := H) ⋙ Rep.indFunctor Complex a.toHom) ⋙
    Rep.toModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := Complex) (G := G)

private noncomputable abbrev strandRes {H G : Subgroup U} (a : ConjEmbedding H G) :
    Func.{u,v} H G :=
  ModuleCat.restrictScalars (strandPhi a).toRingHom

private theorem strandIsos {H G : Subgroup U} (a : ConjEmbedding H G) :
    Nonempty (T.{u,v} (Word.up a) ≅ strandInd a) ∧
    Nonempty (T.{u,v} (Word.down a) ≅ strandRes a) := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := a.hasRepresentative
  have hmem (h : H) : α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G := hα h ▸ (a.toHom h).property
  have ha : a = ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hmem :=
    ConjEmbedding.ext (MonoidHom.ext fun h => Subtype.ext (hα h))
  rw [ha]
  let a := ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hmem
  obtain ⟨I, D, hIleft, hIright, hDleft, hDright, hIgroup, hDgroup, hInd, hRes⟩ :=
    (InductionRestrictionBimoduleStrands.{u,v,u}).1 H G α hmem |>.2.2
  let eu := wordCoeffIso.{u,v} (G := G) (Word.up a) rfl
  let ed := wordCoeffIso.{u,v} (G := G) (Word.down a) rfl
  have upGroup (k : G) (h : H) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} (Word.up a)) :
      eu ((wordBimod (Word.up a)).ρ (k, h⁻¹) b) =
        AlgHom.id Complex (MonoidAlgebra Complex G) (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex G k) *
          (eu b * strandPhi a (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex H h)) := by
    change MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
        (Biset.actLinear Complex (Word.up a).basis (k, h⁻¹) (lower (Word.up a) b)) =
      MonoidAlgebra.single k 1 * (eu b * strandPhi a (MonoidAlgebra.single h 1))
    have hcoeff : (eu b).coeff = lower (Word.up a) b := rfl
    have hg := hIgroup k h (eu b)
    rw [hIleft, hIright, hcoeff] at hg
    exact hg
  have downGroup (h : H) (k : G) (b : wordBimod.{u,v} (Word.down a)) :
      ed ((wordBimod (Word.down a)).ρ (h, k⁻¹) b) =
        strandPhi a (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex H h) *
          (ed b * AlgHom.id Complex (MonoidAlgebra Complex G) (MonoidAlgebra.of Complex G k)) := by
    change MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
        (Biset.actLinear Complex (Word.down a).basis (h, k⁻¹) (lower (Word.down a) b)) =
      strandPhi a (MonoidAlgebra.single h 1) * (ed b * MonoidAlgebra.single k 1)
    have hcoeff : (ed b).coeff = lower (Word.down a) b := rfl
    have hg := hDgroup h k (ed b)
    rw [hDleft, hDright, hcoeff] at hg
    exact hg
  obtain ⟨ul, ur⟩ := strandActions eu (AlgHom.id _ _) (strandPhi a) upGroup
  obtain ⟨dl, dr⟩ := strandActions ed (strandPhi a) (AlgHom.id _ _) downGroup
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := hInd
  obtain ⟨τ, hτ⟩ := hRes
  have hu : StrandPresentation (F := strandInd.{u,v} a)
      (fun s b => s * b) (fun r b => b * strandPhi a r) σ := by
    simpa only [StrandPresentation, StrandBalanced, hIleft, hIright] using hσ
  have hd : StrandPresentation (F := strandRes.{u,v} a)
      (fun r b => strandPhi a r * b) (fun s b => b * s) τ := by
    simpa only [StrandPresentation, StrandBalanced, hDleft, hDright] using hτ
  exact ⟨⟨strand_iso eu ul ur (wordPresentation (Word.up a)) hu⟩,
         ⟨strand_iso ed dl dr (wordPresentation (Word.down a)) hd⟩⟩

end DiagramFunctorProof

#print axioms DiagramFunctorProof.emptyIso
#print axioms DiagramFunctorProof.emptyIso_pure
#print axioms DiagramFunctorProof.strandIsos

import Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.Induced
import Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.Rep.Iso
import Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ModuleCat
import Mathlib.GroupTheory.QuotientGroup.Defs
import MackeyDiagrams.Embedding

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits Representation
open scoped MonoidAlgebra TensorProduct

namespace DiagramFunctorProof

universe u v
noncomputable section

variable {H G : Type u} [Group H] [Group G] (f : H →* G)

-- This is the coset key bijection used in freeRight. Invert the labels
-- in IndV, whose coinvariant presentation uses the left regular action.
private def cosetKeys (hf : Function.Injective f) : (Σ _ : G ⧸ f.range, H) ≃ G :=
  Equiv.ofBijective (fun ih => Quotient.out ih.1 * f ih.2) (by
    have quotient_eq (i : G ⧸ f.range) (h : H) :
        ((Quotient.out i * f h : G) : G ⧸ f.range) = i := by
      refine (QuotientGroup.eq.mpr ?_).trans (Quotient.out_eq' i)
      exact ⟨h⁻¹, by simp [mul_inv_rev, mul_assoc]⟩
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, h⟩ ⟨j, k⟩ (e : Quotient.out i * f h = Quotient.out j * f k)
      have eqij : i = j := (quotient_eq i h).symm.trans
        ((congrArg (fun x : G => (x : G ⧸ f.range)) e).trans (quotient_eq j k))
      subst j
      congr 1
      exact hf (mul_left_cancel e)
    · intro g
      let i : G ⧸ f.range := (g : G ⧸ f.range)
      have eqi : ((Quotient.out i : G) : G ⧸ f.range) = (g : G ⧸ f.range) :=
        Quotient.out_eq' i
      obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := QuotientGroup.eq.mp eqi
      exact ⟨⟨i, h⟩, by change Quotient.out i * f h = g; rw [hh, mul_inv_cancel_left]⟩)

private theorem cosetKeys_apply (hf : Function.Injective f) (i : G ⧸ f.range) (h : H) :
    cosetKeys f hf ⟨i, h⟩ = Quotient.out i * f h := rfl

variable (hf : Function.Injective f) (A : Rep.{max u v} ℂ H)

private def indCoordinate (g : G) : A →ₗ[ℂ] (G ⧸ f.range →₀ A) :=
  let ih := (cosetKeys f hf).symm g⁻¹
  Finsupp.lsingle ih.1 ∘ₗ A.ρ ih.2

private theorem indCoordinate_onKey (i : G ⧸ f.range) (h : H) (x : A) :
    indCoordinate f hf A (Quotient.out i * f h)⁻¹ x =
      Finsupp.single i (A.ρ h x) := by
  simp [indCoordinate, ← cosetKeys_apply f hf]

private theorem indCoordinate_balance (s : H) (g : G) (x : A) :
    indCoordinate f hf A (f s * g) (A.ρ s x) = indCoordinate f hf A g x := by
  obtain ⟨⟨i, h⟩, hg⟩ := (cosetKeys f hf).surjective g⁻¹
  have hg' : g = (Quotient.out i * f h)⁻¹ := by
    simpa [cosetKeys_apply] using (congrArg Inv.inv hg).symm
  rw [hg', indCoordinate_onKey]
  have ha : f s * (Quotient.out i * f h)⁻¹ = (Quotient.out i * f (h * s⁻¹))⁻¹ := by
    simp [mul_inv_rev, mul_assoc]
  rw [ha, indCoordinate_onKey]
  simp

private def indToCoordinates : IndV f A.ρ →ₗ[ℂ] (G ⧸ f.range →₀ A) :=
  Coinvariants.lift _
    (TensorProduct.lift <| (Finsupp.lift (A →ₗ[ℂ] (G ⧸ f.range →₀ A)) ℂ G (indCoordinate f hf A)) ∘ₗ
      (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv ℂ).toLinearMap) (by
        intro s
        ext g x i
        simpa [ofMulAction_single] using
          DFunLike.congr_fun (indCoordinate_balance f hf A s g x) i)

private theorem indToCoordinates_mk (g : G) (x : A) :
    indToCoordinates f hf A (IndV.mk f A.ρ g x) = indCoordinate f hf A g x := by
  simp [indToCoordinates, IndV.mk]

private def indFromCoordinates : (G ⧸ f.range →₀ A) →ₗ[ℂ] IndV f A.ρ :=
  Finsupp.lsum ℂ fun i => IndV.mk f A.ρ (Quotient.out i)⁻¹

private theorem indFromCoordinates_single (i : G ⧸ f.range) (x : A) :
    indFromCoordinates f A (Finsupp.single i x) = IndV.mk f A.ρ (Quotient.out i)⁻¹ x := by
  exact Finsupp.lsum_single _ _ i x

private theorem indMk_onKey (i : G ⧸ f.range) (h : H) (x : A) :
    IndV.mk f A.ρ (Quotient.out i * f h)⁻¹ x =
      IndV.mk f A.ρ (Quotient.out i)⁻¹ (A.ρ h x) := by
  simpa [IndV.mk, LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, TensorProduct.mk_apply, mul_inv_rev]
    using Coinvariants.mk_inv_tmul ((leftRegular ℂ G).comp f) A.ρ
      (MonoidAlgebra.single (Quotient.out i)⁻¹ 1) x h

private theorem indFromTo :
    (indFromCoordinates f A).comp (indToCoordinates f hf A) = LinearMap.id := by
  apply IndV.hom_ext f A.ρ
  intro g
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  change indFromCoordinates f A (indToCoordinates f hf A (IndV.mk f A.ρ g x)) =
    IndV.mk f A.ρ g x
  obtain ⟨⟨i, h⟩, hg⟩ := (cosetKeys f hf).surjective g⁻¹
  have hg' : g = (Quotient.out i * f h)⁻¹ := by
    simpa [cosetKeys_apply] using (congrArg Inv.inv hg).symm
  rw [hg', indToCoordinates_mk, indCoordinate_onKey, indFromCoordinates_single, indMk_onKey]

private theorem indToFrom :
    (indToCoordinates f hf A).comp (indFromCoordinates f A) = LinearMap.id := by
  apply Finsupp.lhom_ext
  intro i x

articleResults.title: Eilenberg–Watts [1, 2]

article.statement:
For unital rings \(R,S\), there is an equivalence from \(\Bimod(S,R)\)
to the category of additive, right-exact functors \(R\Mod\to S\Mod\)
that preserve all set-indexed coproducts, with natural transformations
as morphisms. It sends
\[
  B\longmapsto B\otimes_R-,\qquad f\longmapsto f\otimes_R\id .
\]
Its quasi-inverse sends \(F\) to \(F({}_R R)\) and \(\theta\) to
\(\theta_R\). For \(b\in F(R)\) and \(r\in R\), the right action is
\(br=F(\rho_r)(b)\), where \(\rho_r(x)=xr\). For composable bimodules
\(B\in\Bimod(S,R)\) and \(C\in\Bimod(T,S)\), composition corresponds to
\(C\otimes_S B\), and the identity corresponds to the regular bimodule.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 1.1 [thm:ew], p. 2

articleResults.title: Complex-linear Eilenberg–Watts correspondence

article.statement:
For \(\C\)-algebras the equivalence identifies bimodules with equal
scalar actions with \(\C\)-linear functors of the stated kind.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.1, unnumbered, p. 2

articleResults.title: Correspondence via small projective generators

article.statement:
Let \(\mathcal A,\mathcal E\) be locally small abelian categories with
all set-indexed coproducts and small projective generators \(P,Q\).
Here small means that \(\Hom(P,-)\) or \(\Hom(Q,-)\) preserves those
coproducts. Put \(R=\End_{\mathcal A}(P)^\op\) and
\(S=\End_{\mathcal E}(Q)^\op\). The Hom functors give equivalences
\(\mathcal A\simeq R\Mod\) and \(\mathcal E\simeq S\Mod\)
[2, Chs.~8--10]. Theorem~1.1 then sends \(F\) to
\(\Hom_{\mathcal E}(Q,F(P))\), with actions
\[
 q^\op b p^\op=F(p)\circ b\circ q.
\]
A natural transformation acts by postcomposition with its component
at \(P\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.1, unnumbered, p. 2

articleResults.title: Conjugation embeddings and their centralizer cosets

article.statement:
Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

articleResults.title: Dual-basis identities and reverse triangle identities

article.statement:
Define the \(\C[H]\)-bimodule trace
\[
 E_\alpha(g)=
 \begin{cases}
 \alpha^{-1}g\alpha,&g\in\cg{\alpha}{H},\\
 0,&g\notin\cg{\alpha}{H},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad g\in G,
\]
and extend it linearly. When \([G:\cg{\alpha}{H}]<\infty\), choose
\(T\subseteq G\) with \(G=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}\cg{\alpha}{H}\,t\).
The reverse adjunction \(\Res_{\alpha_*}\dashv\Ind_{\alpha_*}\) has
unit and counit
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tu &: \C[G]\longrightarrow \I\otimes_{\C[H]}\D,\qquad
           g\longmapsto \sum_{t\in T}g t^{-1}\otimes t
                      =\sum_{t\in T}t^{-1}\otimes t g,\\
 \tv &: \D\otimes_{\C[G]}\I\longrightarrow \C[H],\qquad
           x\otimes y\longmapsto E_\alpha(xy).
 \end{aligned}
\]

The dual-basis identities are
\[
 \sum_{t\in T}t^{-1}\alpha_*\bigl(E_\alpha(t x)\bigr)=x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t\in T}\alpha_*\bigl(E_\alpha(x t^{-1})\bigr)t=x .
\]
For a basis element \(x\in G\), each identity has exactly one
nonzero term, by the decompositions using \(T\) and \(T^{-1}\).
They give the two reverse triangle identities. The trace cap is
defined at every index. The reverse unit displayed above is part of
the generating calculus at finite index.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.2, Cups and caps, p. 3

articleResults.title: Correspondence with the diagram-generated functor category

article.statement:
For fixed endpoints \(K,H\), the objects of \(\mathcal D_U(K,H)\)
are sequences of strands from \(H\) to \(K\), interpreted as tensor
products. When \(K=H\), the empty sequence gives the regular bimodule.
Maps are built from dots, cups, caps, merges, splits, identities,
and the associativity and unit maps for tensor products. We allow
tensor product, composition, and finite \(\C\)-linear combinations of
maps with the same source and target. Equal evaluated maps define
the same morphism. One may also include finite direct sums and
matrices of maps. Section~2 uses the full bimodule
category for arbitrary direct sums.

Eilenberg--Watts identifies \(\C[K]\)-\(\C[H]\) bimodules with equal
scalar actions with \(\C\)-linear, right-exact, coproduct-preserving
functors from \(\C[H]\Mod\) to \(\C[K]\Mod\). Bimodule maps
correspond to natural transformations.

The category \(\mathcal D_U(K,H)\) corresponds to composites of the
given inductions and restrictions. Its transformations are built
from the indicated maps by tensor product, composition, and finite
linear combination. For a transformation between two such tensor
functors, membership is determined by its component at \(\C[H]\),
using the tensor unit identifications. Finite direct sums and
matrices of maps correspond on both sides.

These composite functors are exact and preserve coproducts.
Restriction acts on the same vector spaces, and \(\C[G]\) is free as
a right \(\C[H]\)-module along each embedding. Allowing every bimodule
map would give the full subcategory on these functors.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.3, unnumbered, p. 4

articleResults.title: Ordinary Mackey decomposition [3]

article.statement:
Let \(K,H\le G\) be subgroups with their given inclusions. Set
\(I=K\backslash G/H\), the set of double cosets
\(KgH=\{kgh:k\in K,\ h\in H\}\) for \(g\in G\).
Choose an indexed family \((\sigma_i)_{i\in I}\) in \(G\) with
\(\sigma_i\in i\) for each \(i\). Thus \(i=K\sigma_i H\) and
\[
 G=\bigsqcup_{i\in I}K\sigma_i H .
\]
For each \(i\in I\), set \(L_i=K\cap\sigma_i H\sigma_i^{-1}\).
Use the inclusion \(L_i\hookrightarrow K\) and the embedding
\(\mu_i:L_i\hookrightarrow H\) given by \(\ell\mapsto\sigma_i^{-1}\ell\sigma_i\).
Then there is a natural isomorphism
\[
 \Res_K^G\,\Ind_H^G
    \ \cong\ \bigoplus_{i\in I}\Ind_{L_i}^K\,\Res_{\mu_i}.
\]
At the bimodule level the map from the \(i\)-th summand
\(\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_i]}\C[H]\) to \(\C[G]\) takes
\(k\otimes h\) to \(k\sigma_i h\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 2.1 [thm:ordinary-mackey], p. 5

articleResults.title: Generalized Mackey decomposition

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

There are bimodule maps \(p_j:M\to M_j\) and \(\iota_j:M_j\to M\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:split}
   \id_M=\sum_{j\in J}\iota_j\circ p_j,\qquad
   p_j\circ\iota_i=
   \begin{cases}
     \id_{M_i},&i=j,\\
     0,&i\ne j.
   \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The sum is pointwise finite and gives
\[
 M\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}M_j,\qquad
 \Res_{\alpha_*}\,\Ind_{\beta_*}
   \cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}\Ind_{\lambda_j}\,\Res_{\mu_j}.
\]
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 2.2 [thm:mackey]; (2.1) [eq:conj-cosets], (2.2) [eq:alt-L], (2.3) [eq:split], p. 5

articleResults.title: The surviving coset representative

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

For each \(j\), choose right coset representatives \(h_u\) indexed by
\(U_j\), so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H-cosets}
 H=\bigsqcup_{u\in U_j}(\cg{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}{L_j})h_u .
\end{equation}
For \(g\in G\), put
\[
 U'_j(g)=\{u\in U_j:
   \alpha^{-1}g\beta h_u^{-1}\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\alpha\in K\}.
\]

The set \(U'_j(g)\) has exactly one element if \(g\in j\) and is
empty otherwise.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Lemma 2.3 [lem:first-filter]; (2.4) [eq:H-cosets], p. 6

articleResults.title: Composite on a double-coset summand

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

For each \(j\), choose right coset representatives \(h_u\) indexed by
\(U_j\), so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H-cosets}
 H=\bigsqcup_{u\in U_j}(\cg{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}{L_j})h_u .
\end{equation}
For \(g\in G\), put
\[
 U'_j(g)=\{u\in U_j:
   \alpha^{-1}g\beta h_u^{-1}\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\alpha\in K\}.
\]

The dot \(\sigma_j\) and the multiplication cap give
\[
 \iota_j(k\otimes h)=\alpha k\alpha^{-1}\sigma_j\beta h\beta^{-1}.
\]
This formula is balanced because
\(\alpha_*(\lambda_j(\ell))=\ell\) and
\(\sigma_j\beta_*(\mu_j(\ell))=\ell\sigma_j\) for \(\ell\in L_j\).
It commutes with the left \(K\)-action and the right \(H\)-action.

For the other crossing, the reverse cup supplies the coset terms,
the dot inserts \(\sigma_j^{-1}\), and the trace
\(E_\alpha:\C[G]\to\C[K]\) keeps only the indices in \(U'_j(g)\). Thus
\[
 p_j(g)=\sum_{u\in U'_j(g)}
   \alpha^{-1}g\beta h_u^{-1}\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\alpha\otimes h_u .
\]
Extend this formula linearly. If the coset index in (2.4)
is infinite, apply the trace term by term. Lemma~2.3
gives at most one term on each basis element.

Apply \(\iota_j\) to each surviving term. The dot \(\sigma_j\)
cancels \(\sigma_j^{-1}\), and \(h_u^{-1}h_u=1\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:first-chain}
 (\iota_j\circ p_j)(g)=|U'_j(g)|\,g .
\end{equation}
By Lemma~2.3, this fixes \(g\) if \(g\in j\)
and sends it to zero otherwise. Each \(g\in G\) lies in exactly one
double coset. Summing over \(j\) gives \(\id_M\), and the sum is
finite on each input.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 2.2, (2.5) [eq:first-chain] in the proof of Theorem 2.2, pp. 6–7

articleResults.title: Right curl and dot slide

article.statement:
The right curl on \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) uses the
reverse cup and multiplication cap for the embedding by \(\delta\)
of \(K\) into \(H\). It requires \([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]<\infty\).
For the inclusion this index is \([H:K]\).

The curl multiplies by \([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\).
For \(d=\alpha\beta^{-1}\in G\), the dot \(r_d(x)=xd\) changes
\(\bar\alpha\) to \(\bar\beta\). Using the same embedding of \(K\)
into \(H\), the dot below, inside, or above the curl gives
\(x\mapsto[H:\cg{\delta}{K}]xd\).

For the four identities below take \(\gamma,\gamma'\) for embeddings
of \(H\) into \(G\) and \(\alpha,\beta\) for embeddings of \(K\) into \(H\).
Set \(d=\gamma(\gamma')^{-1}\in G\) and \(e=\alpha\beta^{-1}\in H\).
Write \(m_{\gamma,\alpha}\) and \(m^\downarrow_{\gamma,\alpha}\) for the
induction and restriction merges and \(\ell_a(x)=ax\).
The identities are in order for the induction merge, induction split,
restriction merge, and restriction split.
\begin{align}
 m_{\gamma',\beta}\circ(r_d\otimes r_e)
  &=r_{d\gamma'e(\gamma')^{-1}}\circ m_{\gamma,\alpha},
       \label{eq:two-leg-slide}\\
 (r_d\otimes r_e)\circ m_{\gamma,\alpha}^{-1}
  &=m_{\gamma',\beta}^{-1}\circ r_{d\gamma'e(\gamma')^{-1}},\\
 m^\downarrow_{\gamma',\beta}\circ(\ell_{e^{-1}}\otimes\ell_{d^{-1}})
  &=\ell_{\gamma'e^{-1}(\gamma')^{-1}d^{-1}}\circ
        m^\downarrow_{\gamma,\alpha},\\
 (\ell_{e^{-1}}\otimes\ell_{d^{-1}})\circ(m^\downarrow_{\gamma,\alpha})^{-1}
  &=(m^\downarrow_{\gamma',\beta})^{-1}\circ
        \ell_{\gamma'e^{-1}(\gamma')^{-1}d^{-1}} .
\end{align}
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.1 [prop:curl]; (3.1) [eq:two-leg-slide], (3.2)–(3.4), p. 7 (related source excerpts on pp. 7–8)

articleResults.title: Curl with a dot centralizing the internal group

article.statement:
The right curl on \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) uses the
reverse cup and multiplication cap for the embedding by \(\delta\)
of \(K\) into \(H\). It requires \([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]<\infty\).
For the inclusion this index is \([H:K]\).

Choose \(T\) with \(H=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}(\cg{\delta}{K})t\).

A curl with a dot \(a\in \C[H]\) commuting with \(\C[\cg{\delta}{K}]\)
on its induction factor acts by right multiplication by
\[
 \alpha_*\!\left(\sum_{t\in T}t^{-1}at\right).
\]
This follows by inserting \(a\) between \(t^{-1}\) and \(t\).
Replacing \(t\) by \(\ell t\), \(\ell\in\cg{\delta}{K}\), leaves
the summand unchanged. Right multiplication permutes the cosets,
so the sum is central in \(\C[H]\). A dot between the \(\alpha_*\)
and \(\beta_*\) strands intertwines their images of this sum.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.1, unnumbered, p. 8

articleResults.title: Moving a merged dot to an input branch

article.statement:
For the four identities below take \(\gamma,\gamma'\) for embeddings
of \(H\) into \(G\) and \(\alpha,\beta\) for embeddings of \(K\) into \(H\).
Set \(d=\gamma(\gamma')^{-1}\in G\) and \(e=\alpha\beta^{-1}\in H\).
Write \(m_{\gamma,\alpha}\) and \(m^\downarrow_{\gamma,\alpha}\) for the
induction and restriction merges and \(\ell_a(x)=ax\).
The identities are in order for the induction merge, induction split,
restriction merge, and restriction split.

Fix the incoming labels of a merge. A dot \(D\in G\) on its merged
strand can move to the right input exactly when \(D\in\cg{\gamma}{H}\).
Necessity follows from (3.1) with \(d=1\).
For sufficiency take \(e=\gamma^{-1}D\gamma\in H\) and
\(\beta=e^{-1}\alpha\). This embeds \(K\) into \(H\) and gives the
same output embedding, since both conjugate \((\gamma\alpha)_*\)
by \(D^{-1}\). A dot can always move to the left input by taking
\(\gamma'=D^{-1}\gamma\) and \(e=1\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, Moving a dot back to a branch, p. 9

articleResults.title: Moving a split dot to an output branch

article.statement:
For the four identities below take \(\gamma,\gamma'\) for embeddings
of \(H\) into \(G\) and \(\alpha,\beta\) for embeddings of \(K\) into \(H\).
Set \(d=\gamma(\gamma')^{-1}\in G\) and \(e=\alpha\beta^{-1}\in H\).
Write \(m_{\gamma,\alpha}\) and \(m^\downarrow_{\gamma,\alpha}\) for the
induction and restriction merges and \(\ell_a(x)=ax\).
The identities are in order for the induction merge, induction split,
restriction merge, and restriction split.

For a split with left label \(\bar\alpha\), moving a dot to the
right output requires \(D\in\cg{\alpha}{H}\). To move it to the
left output, factor the given input representative \(b\) as
\((b\gamma^{-1})\gamma\). Since
\(D=b(\alpha\gamma)^{-1}\), the left representative
\(b\gamma^{-1}=D\alpha\) embeds \(H\) into \(G\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, Moving a dot back to a branch, p. 9

articleResults.title: Moving a scalar right curl across a merge or split

article.statement:
A right curl with no dot multiplies by its index. It can move
across a merge or split if the new curl has the same index.
The right input and the merged strand have the same right
region \(K\). The left input has right region \(H\), where
\[
 [H:\cg{\alpha}{L}]=[H:\cg{\alpha}{K}]\,[K:L]
\]
for \(L\le K\) and finite indices.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, Moving a curl across a vertex, p. 9

articleResults.title: Two curls with different indices

article.statement:
For \(G=H=C_2\) and \(K=L=1\),
the curls using \(1\) multiply by \(1\) on the right input and
by \(2\) on the left.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.1 [ex:different-curl-indices], p. 9

articleResults.title: Normalized right curls

article.statement:
Dividing each curl by its finite index
gives the identity.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, unnumbered, p. 9

articleResults.title: Preorder on shapes at fixed boundary

article.statement:
For shapes \(A,B\) with the same boundary shape, write \(A\preceq B\)
if every labelling of \(A\) can be replaced by a labelling of \(B\)
with the same boundary groups, boundary cosets, and map. Internal
labels may change. This is inclusion of the sets of maps at each
fixed boundary, so the relation is reflexive and transitive.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.3, unnumbered, p. 10

articleResults.title: The dot-slide preorder is not symmetric

article.statement:
For shapes \(A,B\) with the same boundary shape, write \(A\preceq B\)
if every labelling of \(A\) can be replaced by a labelling of \(B\)
with the same boundary groups, boundary cosets, and map. Internal
labels may change. This is inclusion of the sets of maps at each
fixed boundary, so the relation is reflexive and transitive.

Let \(A\) be the induction merge with a dot on the right input, and
let \(B\) be the induction merge with a dot on the merged strand. Then
\(A\preceq B\) and \(B\npreceq A\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.2 [prop:preorder-not-symmetric], p. 10

articleResults.title: A dot that cannot move to the right input

article.statement:
Take the standard inclusions in the finitary symmetric group
\[
   K=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2\})\ \le\
   H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3\})\ \le\
   G=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3,4\}).
\]
Fix all boundary strands to be these inclusions and their composite.
Put \(g=(3\,4)\) on the merged strand of \(B\). It centralizes
\(K\), so \(g,1\) represent the same label there. The map sends
\(1\otimes1\) to \(g\). In shape \(A\), the image of \(1\otimes1\)
is the right-input label and lies in \(H\), whereas \(g\notin H\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.2 [ex:dot-slide-obstruction], p. 10

articleResults.title: Orbit-sum basis for induction-bimodule maps

article.statement:
Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

The up and down strands below denote
\[
 \I_{\co\alpha}^{G,H}={}_{\C[G]}(\C[G])_{\alpha_*,\C[H]},\qquad
 \D_{\co\alpha}^{H,G}={}_{\C[H],\alpha_*}(\C[G])_{\C[G]}.
\]
The actions are \(x\cdot h=x\alpha h\alpha^{-1}\) on \(\I\) and
\(h\cdot x=\alpha h\alpha^{-1}x\) on \(\D\). Tensoring on the right
gives induction and restriction, respectively. The target group
is on the left. Read horizontal composition as tensor product over
the middle group and vertical composition from bottom to top.

The space of bimodule maps from \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) to
\(\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\) has a basis given by right multiplication
by the sums of the finite orbits of
\[
       h\cdot g=\alpha_*(h)g\,\beta_*(h)^{-1}
       \qquad(h\in H,\ g\in G).
\]
The single group-element dots are the singleton orbits. If \(H\) is
finite, the sum over each orbit is realized by a diagram.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.3 [prop:orbit-hom], p. 10

articleResults.title: Orbit-sum diagram from a reverse cup and multiplication cap

article.statement:
The space of bimodule maps from \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) to
\(\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\) has a basis given by right multiplication
by the sums of the finite orbits of
\[
       h\cdot g=\alpha_*(h)g\,\beta_*(h)^{-1}
       \qquad(h\in H,\ g\in G).
\]
The single group-element dots are the singleton orbits. If \(H\) is
finite, the sum over each orbit is realized by a diagram.

For finite \(H\), insert the reverse cup for \(1\hookrightarrow H\)
on the right of the \(\bar\alpha\)-strand. Merge the two induction
strands to an induction from \(1\) to \(G\), put the dot \(g\) on
that strand, then split using the \(\bar\beta\)-strand and apply the
multiplication cap for \(1\hookrightarrow H\). The resulting value
at \(x\) is
\[
 x\sum_{t\in H}\alpha_*(t^{-1})g\beta_*(t)
   =x\,|\operatorname{Stab}_H(g)|\sum_{z\in H\cdot g}z .
\]
The stabilizer order is invertible in \(\C\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 10

articleResults.title: A block swap

article.statement:
Let
\[
 B_1=\{1,2,3\},\quad B_2=\{4,5,6\},\quad
 B_3=\{7,8,9\},\quad B_4=\{10,11,12\}.
\]
Put
\[
 G=\operatorname{Sym}(B_1\cup B_2)\times\operatorname{Sym}(B_3\cup B_4),
 \qquad H=\prod_{i=1}^4\operatorname{Sym}(B_i).
\]
Take \(\alpha=(4\,7)(5\,8)(6\,9)\) and \(\beta=1\).
The embeddings send \((4\,5)\) to transpositions in different
\(G\)-blocks. Every element of \(G\) preserves the two blocks,
so there is no group-element dot between these embeddings.
The sum over the orbit of \(1\) gives a nonzero diagram map by
Proposition~3.3.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.3 [ex:block-swap], p. 10

articleResults.title: Blockwise criterion for group-element dots

article.statement:
Suppose \(H,G\) are products of symmetric groups on disjoint
blocks in the group of finitely supported permutations. Each
embedding sends a non-singleton \(H\)-block into a \(G\)-block.
A dot exists exactly when the two images of each non-singleton
\(H\)-block lie in the same \(G\)-block. Necessity follows by
testing transpositions. For sufficiency extend
\(\beta(x)\mapsto\alpha(x)\) on those images to permutations in
the \(G\)-blocks. These partial bijections differ from the
identity at finitely many points, so the extensions can have
finite support. Together they give a dot in \(G\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, A criterion for group-element dots, p. 11

articleResults.title: A dot between two images in one block

article.statement:
\(1\) and \((2\,3)\) send \(\{1,2\}\) to different
sets in \(S_4\), and \((2\,3)\) gives a dot.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.4 [ex:dot-in-one-block], p. 11

articleResults.title: A reverse slide under the stronger embedding condition

article.statement:
Fix a representative \(\beta\) for the embedding of \(K\) into \(H\).
Suppose \(\cg{\sigma\beta^{-1}}{H}\le G\) whenever
\(\cg{\sigma}{K}\le G\). A reverse slide onto the right leg
can still fail.

Use
\(K=\prod_i\operatorname{Sym}(B_i)\),
\(H=\operatorname{Sym}(B_1\cup B_2)\times\operatorname{Sym}(B_3\cup B_4)\),
\(G=S_{\{1,\ldots,12\}}\), and \(\beta=1\). If
\(\cg{\sigma}{K}\le G\), the support of \(\cg{\sigma}{K}\) forces
\(\sigma\) to preserve \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\), so
\(\cg{\sigma}{H}\le G\). The block swap \(\alpha=(4\,7)(5\,8)(6\,9)\)
conjugates \(K\) to itself and lies in \(G\setminus H\).
It labels a dot on the merged strand from the inclusion to
\(\bar\alpha\). It cannot move to the right input because it lies
outside \(H\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.5 [ex:stronger-slide-obstruction], p. 11

articleResults.title: Support bounds under composition

article.statement:
For a finite subgroup \(X\) given by symmetric groups on disjoint
blocks, let \(\operatorname{supp}X\) be the union of its non-singleton blocks
and \(\widehat X=\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{supp}X)\). The conditions
\(\alpha\in G\widehat H\) and \(\beta\in H\widehat K\) do not ensure
\(\alpha\beta\in G\widehat K\).

Take
\[
 G=H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,6\})
         \times\operatorname{Sym}(\{7,\ldots,12\}),
 \qquad K=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3\}).
\]
Let \(\alpha\) swap the two six-point blocks and let \(\beta=1\).
The two embeddings satisfy the support bounds.
Every element of \(G\widehat K\) preserves each six-point block,
whereas \(\alpha\beta\) carries the support of \(K\) into the second
block. Even the composite strand label has no representative
in \(G\widehat K\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.6 [ex:support-composite], p. 11

articleResults.title: Support bounds for an inverse product

article.statement:
Consider whether \(\cg{\beta\alpha^{-1}}{H}\le G\)
when \(\alpha,\beta\in\widehat G H\) both embed \(H\) in \(G\). Take \(G\) to be the product of the symmetric groups on
\(\{1,2\},\{3,4\},\{5,6\}\), \(H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2\})\),
\(\alpha=(1\,3)(2\,4)\), and \(\beta=(4\,5)\).
Both permutations belong to \(\widehat G H\) and embed \(H\) in \(G\).
But \(\beta\alpha^{-1}\) sends \(\{1,2\}\) to \(\{3,5\}\), so
\(\cg{\beta\alpha^{-1}}{H}\nleq G\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.7 [ex:support-inverse-product], p. 11

articleResults.title: Bend identities

article.statement:
Let \(K\xrightarrow{\alpha_*}H\xrightarrow{\gamma_*}G\)
be conjugation embeddings. The two diagrams in each pair below
give the same bimodule map. The multiplication-cap and ordinary-cup
identities hold at all indices. The trace-cap identity holds when
\([H:\cg{\alpha}{K}]<\infty\), and the reverse-cup identity holds when
\([G:\cg{\gamma\alpha}{K}]<\infty\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.4 [prop:trivalent-bends]; four unnumbered diagrams, p. 12

articleResults.title: Reidemeister I

article.statement:
Use \(K\xrightarrow{\delta_*}H\xrightarrow{\alpha_*}G\).
The subscript on \(\id\) lists the groups on the left and right.

The four curls shown below satisfy
\begin{align}
 \text{right curl on an up-strand}   &=
       [H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\,\id_{G\cdot H}, \label{eq:curl-right-up}\\
 \text{right curl on a down-strand} &=
       \id_{K\cdot H}, \label{eq:curl-right-down}\\
 \text{left curl on an up-strand}    &=
       \id_{H\cdot K}, \label{eq:curl-left-up}\\
 \text{left curl on a down-strand}   &=
       [H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\,\id_{H\cdot G}. \label{eq:curl-left-down}
\end{align}
The \(K\)-loops require finite \([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\).
The \(G\)-loops hold at arbitrary index.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 4.1 [thm:reidemeister-one]; (4.1)–(4.4), p. 14

articleResults.title: Normalized index-valued Reidemeister curls

article.statement:
Use \(K\xrightarrow{\delta_*}H\xrightarrow{\alpha_*}G\).
The subscript on \(\id\) lists the groups on the left and right.

Over \(\C\), dividing either \(K\)-loop by its finite index
\([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\) gives the identity.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 4, unnumbered, p. 15

articleResults.title: Two crossings with opposite orientations

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

Use \(J,\sigma_j,L_j,M,M_j\) from Section~2.2.
The two boundary strands of \(M\) point in opposite directions,
with \(G\) between them. To allow a different middle group, take
\(\cg{a}{L}\le K\), \(\cg{b}{L}\le H\) and
\(s=\alpha a(\beta b)^{-1}\in G\). Use \(s,s^{-1}\) as the two
crossing labels and put
\[
 M_L=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L]}\C[H],\qquad
 L_s=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\cap(\cg{s\beta}{H}),\qquad
 n=[L_s:\cg{\alpha a}{L}].
\]
The tensor product has basis \(K\times_L H\), the classes \([k,h]\)
of pairs under \([ka\ell a^{-1},h]=[k,b\ell b^{-1}h]\),
\(\ell\in L\). The relation identifies exactly the pairs equated
by balancing the tensor product.

Suppose \(n<\infty\). Let \(p_L:M\to M_L\) and \(\iota_L:M_L\to M\)
be the two crossings. Write
\(q([k,h])=\alpha k\alpha^{-1}s\beta h\beta^{-1}\).
If \(s\in j\), then
\[
 \iota_L\circ p_L=nP_j,\qquad
 p_L\circ\iota_L(z)=\sum_{q(w)=q(z)}w \quad(z\in K\times_L H),
\]
where \(P_j\) fixes the basis elements in \(j\) and sends the others
to zero. The second composite is the identity exactly when \(n=1\).
For \(n>1\), no scalar multiple of it is the identity.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 5.1 [prop:r2-mixed-composition], p. 15

articleResults.title: Multiplication and projection as a basis map and its finite fiber sum

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

Use \(J,\sigma_j,L_j,M,M_j\) from Section~2.2.
The two boundary strands of \(M\) point in opposite directions,
with \(G\) between them. To allow a different middle group, take
\(\cg{a}{L}\le K\), \(\cg{b}{L}\le H\) and
\(s=\alpha a(\beta b)^{-1}\in G\). Use \(s,s^{-1}\) as the two
crossing labels and put
\[
 M_L=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L]}\C[H],\qquad
 L_s=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\cap(\cg{s\beta}{H}),\qquad
 n=[L_s:\cg{\alpha a}{L}].
\]
The tensor product has basis \(K\times_L H\), the classes \([k,h]\)
of pairs under \([ka\ell a^{-1},h]=[k,b\ell b^{-1}h]\),
\(\ell\in L\). The relation identifies exactly the pairs equated
by balancing the tensor product.

Suppose \(n<\infty\). Let \(p_L:M\to M_L\) and \(\iota_L:M_L\to M\)
be the two crossings. Write
\(q([k,h])=\alpha k\alpha^{-1}s\beta h\beta^{-1}\).
If \(s\in j\), then
\[
 \iota_L\circ p_L=nP_j,\qquad
 p_L\circ\iota_L(z)=\sum_{q(w)=q(z)}w \quad(z\in K\times_L H),
\]
where \(P_j\) fixes the basis elements in \(j\) and sends the others
to zero. The second composite is the identity exactly when \(n=1\).
For \(n>1\), no scalar multiple of it is the identity.

Since \(s\beta b=\alpha a\), conjugation by \(s\) identifies the
two images of \(L\). Thus \(\cg{\alpha a}{L}\le L_s\) and \(q\)
respects the relation on pairs. The dot \(s\) and multiplication
cap give \(\iota_L([k,h])=q([k,h])\).

Choose \(T\) with \(H=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}(\cg{b}{L})t\).
The reverse cup supplies \(t^{-1}\otimes t\), the dot multiplies
the first factor by \(s^{-1}\), and the trace \(E_\alpha\) gives
\[
 p_L(g)=\sum_{t\in T}
 E_\alpha\bigl(g\beta t^{-1}\beta^{-1}s^{-1}\bigr)\otimes t .
\]
Each class has a unique representative \((k,t)\) with \(t\in T\).
The trace returns \(k\) exactly when \(q([k,t])=g\).
Hence \(p_L(g)=\sum_{q(w)=g}w\).

The action of \(K\times H\) is
\((k_0,h_0)[k,h]=[k_0k,hh_0^{-1}]\) and
\((k_0,h_0)g=\alpha k_0\alpha^{-1}g\beta h_0^{-1}\beta^{-1}\).
The balanced set is transitive and \(q\) is equivariant with image
\(j\). Sending \((k_0,h_0)\) to \(\alpha k_0\alpha^{-1}\)
identifies the stabilizers of \(s\) and \([1,1]\) with \(L_s\)
and \(\cg{\alpha a}{L}\), respectively. Their index gives \(n\)
preimages for each \(g\in j\). The sums are therefore finite
and define a bimodule map. Applying \(q\) to the sum gives \(ng\)
on \(j\). In the other order the result sums all preimages of
\(q(z)\). If \(n>1\), this includes a basis element besides \(z\).

The reverse cup is a map when \([H:\cg{b}{L}]<\infty\). At infinite
index the formula for \(p_L\) sums only the terms that survive the trace.
It still defines a map for finite \(n\). For infinite \(n\), the sum
on \(g\in j\) has infinite support.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 5.1, proof and finite-support convention after Proposition 5.1, pp. 15–16

articleResults.title: Mixed Reidemeister II cancellation through full Mackey groups

article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 5.1, Mackey cancellation, p. 16

articleResults.title: Transport to the Mackey representative

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

Use \(J,\sigma_j,L_j,M,M_j\) from Section~2.2.
The two boundary strands of \(M\) point in opposite directions,
with \(G\) between them. To allow a different middle group, take
\(\cg{a}{L}\le K\), \(\cg{b}{L}\le H\) and
\(s=\alpha a(\beta b)^{-1}\in G\). Use \(s,s^{-1}\) as the two
crossing labels and put
\[
 M_L=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L]}\C[H],\qquad
 L_s=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\cap(\cg{s\beta}{H}),\qquad
 n=[L_s:\cg{\alpha a}{L}].
\]
The tensor product has basis \(K\times_L H\), the classes \([k,h]\)
of pairs under \([ka\ell a^{-1},h]=[k,b\ell b^{-1}h]\),
\(\ell\in L\). The relation identifies exactly the pairs equated
by balancing the tensor product.

Let \(s=\alpha a(\beta b)^{-1}\in j\) and write
\[
 s=(\alpha k\alpha^{-1})\sigma_j(\beta h\beta^{-1}),
 \qquad k\in K,\quad h\in H.
\]
Then \(L'=\cg{\alpha k^{-1}a}{L}\le L_j\). Use the restrictions of
\(\lambda_j,\mu_j\) for the embeddings of \(L'\). The map
\[
 [x,y]_L\longmapsto[xk,hy]_{L'}
\]
is a bijection respecting the left \(K\)-action and right \(H\)-action.
Its linear extension intertwines the multiplication crossings with
labels \(s,\sigma_j\), and the projection crossings with labels
\(s^{-1},\sigma_j^{-1}\) when their fiber sums are finite.
Moreover, \([L_j:L']=[L_s:\cg{\alpha a}{L}]\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Lemma 5.2 [lem:mackey-transport], p. 16

article.statement:
Let \(K,H,G\le U\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in U\) satisfy
\(\cg{\alpha}{K}\le G\) and \(\cg{\beta}{H}\le G\).
Let \(J=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\backslash G/(\cg{\beta}{H})\). Choose one
representative \(\sigma_j\in j\) for each \(j\in J\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-cosets}
 j=(\cg{\alpha}{K})\sigma_j(\cg{\beta}{H}),
 \qquad G=\bigsqcup_{j\in J}j.
\end{equation}
For each \(j\), set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alt-L}
 L_j=\cg{\alpha}{K}\cap\cg{\sigma_j\beta}{H} .
\end{equation}
The embeddings out of \(L_j\) are
\(\lambda_j(\ell)=\alpha^{-1}\ell\alpha\in K\) and
\(\mu_j(\ell)=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\ell\sigma_j\beta\in H\).
The strand labels for these maps are
\(\overline{\alpha^{-1}}=\alpha^{-1}C_U(L_j)\) and
\(\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}=\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}C_U(L_j)\).

Write \(M={}_{\C[K]}(\C[G])_{\C[H]}\) with actions through \(\alpha_*,\beta_*\),
and \(M_j=\C[K]\otimes_{\C[L_j]}\C[H]\) with actions in the tensor product
through \(\lambda_j,\mu_j\). A boundary with middle region \(G\)
represents \(\D_{\bar\alpha}^{K,G}\otimes_{\C[G]}\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\cong M\);
one with middle region \(L_j\) represents
\(\I_{\overline{\alpha^{-1}}}^{K,L_j}\otimes_{\C[L_j]}
 \D_{\overline{\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}}}^{L_j,H}\cong M_j\).

Restrict the embeddings of \(L_j\) to \(L\le L_j\), and write
\(p_{L,j},\iota_{L,j}\) for the resulting crossings. For finite
\([L_j:L]\), Proposition~5.1 gives
\(\iota_{L,j}\circ p_{L,j}=[L_j:L]\,(\iota_j\circ p_j)\).

For nonempty \(J_0\subseteq J\), the group \(L=\bigcap_{j\in J_0}L_j\)
can be used separately for each \(j\in J_0\). Use
\(\alpha^{-1}\) into \(K\) and \(\beta^{-1}\sigma_j^{-1}\) into \(H\).
The right labels for \(i,j\) agree exactly when
\(\sigma_i\sigma_j^{-1}\in C_U(L)\).
If all \([L_j:L]\) are finite, termwise division gives
\[
 \sum_{j\in J_0}\frac{\iota_{L,j}\circ p_{L,j}}{[L_j:L]}
  = \sum_{j\in J_0}\iota_j\circ p_j .
\]
Also \(p_{L,j}\circ\iota_{L,i}=0\) for \(i\ne j\), since the double
cosets are disjoint. For infinite \(J_0\) the sum of maps is
pointwise finite, with one term on each basis element in the
selected cosets. A finite \(J_0\) gives a sum of diagrams when
the cups exist.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 5.1, Smaller internal groups and intersections, p. 17

articleResults.title: Admissibility of the product and return dots in parallel induction

article.statement:
The bottom, middle, and top chains through \(H,B,H'\) have
composite conjugators \(u=\alpha\beta\), \(v=\gamma\delta\),
and \(w=\alpha'\beta'\).

Two induction crossings labelled \(d,e\), read bottom to top, equal
a merge, a dot \(de\) from \(\bar u\) to \(\bar w\), and a split.
For \(de=1\) the merged labels agree and the dot disappears.
The remaining map is the identity if both boundary sequences agree.
Each group-element label \(d\) has an admissible return label \(d^{-1}\).

The three merges identify the tensor products with copies of
\(\C[G]\), with right actions through \(u_*,v_*,w_*\).
The split and merge on the middle product cancel, leaving
\(x\mapsto xd\mapsto xde\).
For group-element dots \(u^{-1}dv\) and \(v^{-1}ew\) centralize
\(K\), so their product \(u^{-1}de\,w\) does too. The same test
applies to each product of terms in linear labels.
If \(de=1\), then \(u^{-1}w\in C_U(K)\), so the merged strand
stays the same through the dot. If the boundaries agree, the
top split inverts the bottom merge.
Finally \(v^{-1}d^{-1}u=(u^{-1}dv)^{-1}\) proves admissibility
for the return dot. Both products of \(d,d^{-1}\) equal \(1\).
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 5.2, proof of Theorem 5.4, p. 18

articleResults.title: Parallel Reidemeister II for restriction

article.statement:
The bottom, middle, and top chains through \(H,B,H'\) have
composite conjugators \(u=\alpha\beta\), \(v=\gamma\delta\),
and \(w=\alpha'\beta'\).

For two restriction strands, the group-element labels act on the
left, giving \(x\mapsto d^{-1}x\mapsto e^{-1}d^{-1}x=(de)^{-1}x\).
The product label is again \(de\), including for linear labels by
expansion in group elements.

articleResults.title: Orbit diagram from the projected pair stabilizer

article.statement:
Write \(a:A\to G\), \(b:A\to D\), and \(d:F\to D\) for the lower
embeddings and \(c:C\to G\), \(e:C\to E\), and \(f:F\to E\) for the upper ones.
The source basis is \(G\times_A D\) and the target basis is \(G\times_C E\).

Let \(G\times F\) act on each basis by left multiplication by \(G\)
and right multiplication by the inverse of \(F\), using the boundary
embeddings. The action on input--output pairs acts on both coordinates.
A bimodule map has constant matrix coefficient on each orbit.

Choose a representative \(([1,r]_A,[t,s]_C)\) of an orbit.
Let \(P\le F\) be the image of its stabilizer in \(F\).
In detail, \(h\in P\) exactly when there exist \(i(h)\in A,\ k(h)\in C\)
satisfying
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 r d(h)r^{-1}=b(i(h)),\qquad
 s f(h)s^{-1}=e(k(h)),\\
 a(i(h))=t c(k(h))t^{-1}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
These equations describe the stabilizer as the graph
\(\{(a(i(h)),h):h\in P\}\). They also make \(i,k\) conjugation
embeddings. Take \(B'=P,\ j\) the inclusion, and labels \((r,t,s)\).
The displayed equations are the three vertex conditions.

The pairs in the orbit have the form
\[
 \bigl([g',r d(h)]_A,\ [g't,s f(h)]_C\bigr)
 \qquad(g'\in G,\ h\in F).
\]
The source in this pair equals \([g,x]_A\) exactly when
\(g'=ga(\alpha)\) and \(x=b(\alpha)r d(h)\) for some \(\alpha\in A\).
Two such choices give the same pair exactly when they are equivalent
in \(A\times_P F\), by the full stabilizer description.
Thus (6.4) sums each output in
the orbit once. If this orbit has nonzero coefficient in a bimodule
map, it has finitely many outputs over each input, so the lower
projection is defined.

Conversely, (6.4) shows that a
group-element triple contributes to at most one orbit, irrespective
of the chosen internal group. Finite sums and finite linear labels
therefore involve finitely many orbits. The construction gives one
diagram for each orbit of nonzero coefficient. At each input only
finitely many of these diagrams contribute, because an element of
the target has finite support. This gives the asserted expansion.
article.locator: Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 6.3.1, construction in the proof of Theorem 6.7, pp. 25–26
